page: Amazon Web Services t3.2xlarge is a burstable performance instance belonging to the t3 server family, running on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, alongside 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. However, multi-core performance is more robust, with stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores reaching average levels. Memory bandwidth benchmarks for both cached and uncached read/write operations also perform in the average tier. Conversely, data decompression and database operations, such as Redis SET, show weaker performance, and LLM inference tasks are limited, with medium model prompt processing scoring in the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t3.2xlarge offers a resource-dense profile for workloads with variable CPU utilization. Because it utilizes a burstable CPU allocation model, it is highly cost-effective for applications that remain idle or run at low baseline levels but require temporary bursts of compute power. However, sustained high CPU workloads will deplete CPU credits, making this instance less suitable for continuous heavy processing. This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads with bursty CPU patterns, such as development environments, low-to-medium traffic web servers, code repositories, and microservices.
